s1.syndrome_frame: Vasculitic syndrome with purpuric lesions and systemic involvement
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
History of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease
Presented with altered mental status after an unwitnessed fall
Purpuric lesions developed on nose, ear, and extensor surfaces of arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells

shortlist.label: Type I cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and biopsy showing intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi

shortlist.label: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein

shortlist.label: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses

shortlist.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses, but less likely given systemic involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and biopsy findings of intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi are consistent with Type I cryoglobulinemic vasculitis. Additionally, the presence of monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis and hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells on bone marrow biopsy suggest an underlying plasma cell dyscrasia, which is often associated with Type I cryoglobulinemia.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: While the patient has features of multiple myeloma, such as hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and hypercellular marrow with plasma cell dyscrasia, the primary presentation of purpuric lesions and elevated serum cryoglobulin levels points more specifically to a cryoglobulinemic vasculitis.

rejected.label: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: The patient's monoclonal IgG-κ protein and lack of mixed cryoglobulins (which typically involve a mix of monoclonal and polyclonal immunoglobulins) make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by IgM monoclonal gammopathy, which is not present in this patient.

rejected.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and laboratory findings indicate a more specific and severe condition than MGUS.
